name: Passage to the Lava Stair
purpose: A short, low, warming passage from the boat landing to the Lava Stair, where the orange of the glass slide shaft grows at the far end.

ceiling_profile.note: 3 m lava-tube passage, rounded; lowest at the walls. Already the compressed passage (3.5 x 3 m) before the shaft reveal.

portals.note: Lava Stair landing door (layout, bearing 342.6 from the shaft centre).

hero.why: The glass slide tube glowing orange in its shaft, seen through the far door: the whole passage is aimed at it and it is the brightest thing in view. Not placed by this file.

anchored.why: Bronze-and-timber door frame where the passage meets the Lava Stair; it frames the orange shaft.

sightlines.see: Orange glow and the curve of the glass tube through the far door.
Lantern-amber boat landing and a sliver of teal river.

concept.match: From the stair landing looking down into the shaft: the clear tube spiralling down with water glowing orange from the lava behind glass, bronze ring clamps, steam, lanterns on the stair rail.

lights.why: Ankle-height niches that get dimmer and sparser toward the shaft so the orange takes over.
One post lantern at the Lava Stair door (landing dressing).

dressing.why: Small rock only; the passage is narrow.

mood.key: orange shaft glow at the end of a dark tube
mood.palette: dim amber niches, orange lava light, black basalt
mood.mist: Thin warm haze lit orange near the shaft door.

waivers.reason: Borrowed view: the slide tube lies in the shaft beyond the door, outside this corridor.
57 m2 corridor; lanterns every 3-4 m are the dressing.
